description: Two sentences are similar if one can be made equal to the other by inserting a sentence (possibly empty) somewhere. Given two sentences sentence1 and sentence2, return true if they are similar.
examples:
Input: sentence1 = "My name is Haley", sentence2 = "My Haley"
Output: true
Explanation: Insert "name is" between "My" and "Haley".
intuition: If you can insert a sentence in the middle of the shorter one to make it equal to the longer one, then the shorter sentence must be a prefix plus suffix of the longer one. Matching words from both ends reveals whether the gap in the middle is the only difference.
approach: Split both sentences into words. Match words from the front (prefix) and from the back (suffix). If the total matched words cover the shorter sentence, they are similar.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: sentence1 = "My name is Haley", sentence2 = "My Haley"
words1 = ["My","name","is","Haley"] (longer), words2 = ["My","Haley"]
Prefix match: words1[0]="My" == words2[0]="My" -> i=1
  words1[1]="name" != words2[1]="Haley" -> stop. i=1
Suffix match: j can go up to words2.length - i = 2-1 = 1
  j=0: words1[3]="Haley" == words2[1]="Haley" -> j=1
  j=1: limit reached, stop
i + j = 1 + 1 = 2 >= words2.length(2) -> true
explanation:
1. Split sentences into word arrays. Ensure words1 is the longer one.
2. Match words from the beginning (prefix match), counting i matches.
3. Match words from the end (suffix match), counting j matches.
4. If i + j >= len(shorter sentence), the shorter is a prefix+suffix of the longer.
5. The gap in the middle is the "inserted" sentence.
timeComplexity: O(n) where n is total words
hints: Split into words and compare from both ends.
The inserted sentence goes in the middle, so the prefix and suffix must match.
Make sure to handle sentences of different lengths.
